newsitem.title: THAILAND: Bayer reaffirms commitment to Thailand.
newsitem.headline: Bayer reaffirms commitment to Thailand.

text.p: German chemical giant Bayer AG will maintain Thailand as its key Southeast Asian hub despite the country's current economic malaise, a senior company executive said on Friday.
"I think we should not take a momentary situation as the basis for long-term investment," Member of the Board of management Dieter Besher told reporters.
"I am firmly convinced that Thailand will be a stable foothold on Bayer's way to expand its market position particularly in ASEAN and Asia as a whole," he added.
The company has said it will spend 500 million marks investing in Thailand over the next five years.
Thailand is going through its worst economic crisis for decades brought about by slowing economic growth, overborrowing and currency turbulence.

"We at Bayer believe firmly that Thailand has an excellent basis for future industrial expansion and since all our investment is based on long-term strategies we are absolutely confident that we will get the results we expect," Becher said.
Bayer has recently decided to expand its production plants in Thailand with a focus on plastics, raw material Bisphenol A and Tantalum production.
Expansion plans at the firm's Map Ta Phut site on Thailand's eastern seaboard are the firm's single largest investment in Asia.
But the speed of the decline in Thailand's economy had surprised the firm and presented some difficulties, he said.
"I think 18 months ago we were not really aware of coming events," Becher said.

"The turbulence around the baht are a headache not only I think for your country but for the whole international community. On the other hand, I think the whole world has a lot of confidence in the Southeast Asian markets," he added.

Sales in ASEAN, which groups Thailand, Indonesia, Singapore, Brunei, Vietnam, Burma, Malaysia, Laos and the Philippines, rose 10 percent in mark terms in 1996 and contributed more than two percent of Bayer's global revenues.
Sales in Thailand, at 283 million marks in 1996, contributed more than a quarter of total ASEAN revenues, he said.
Sales had continued to grow in Asia as a whole in the first seven months of the year despite continued weakness in the Japanese market, he said.

"In Asia, growth continued despite the persistent softness in the Japanese market. Significant advances during the first half year have been achieved in China, Taiwan, Australia and the ASEAN countries," he said. ($1 = 1.84 marks)
